To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Ihh gene is regulated by at least nine enhancer elements, each with a specific tissue specificity; (2) the individual enhancers act additively to control Ihh expression; (3) duplication of these enhancers leads to gene misexpression, resulting in skeletal abnormalities; and (4) the results of these studies provide insights into the pathophysiology of skeletal malformations in humans.
the IHH enhancer cluster is a multipartite enhancers that controls developmental expression of IHH and alterations in the composition of this enhancer cluster can lead to disease.

enhancers are organized in a complex manner and that their disruption, whether through deletion or duplication, results in misexpression of the gene they control and can cause disease.
